clue.text: Hermit's expert article on living?

definitions.note: read as 'a hermit is': the hermit crab belongs to this class of shelled creatures

indicators.note: in this across clue the expert and the article are placed after, so 'on' the living

parts.note: to earn a crust is to make a living, so a crust is a living
an ace is an expert
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A query about whether a recluse's specialist essay deals with how to make a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hermit' looks like a lonely person, but it is the hermit crab; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hermit crab is an example of this group of shelled, mostly aquatic arthropods.

clue.text: Expense of keeping son in bed

indicators.note: the bed keeps, or holds, the son within it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Complaining about the expense of having a grown son still living at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an expense is the price or outlay something demands.

clue.text: A plug may be so discovered

definitions.meaning: an electrical plug without an earth wire connected is described this way
found by digging up or brought to light

explanation.surface: An electrical plug might be found to have a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' is the British word for the electrical ground wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Dug out of the ground, hence found or brought to light; also lacking a ground connection.

clue.text: Voucher for purchase of no real value

definitions.meaning: a book or gift voucher exchangeable for goods
a gesture that is merely symbolic, as in a nominal payment

explanation.surface: A voucher that turns out to buy nothing worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift voucher is this kind of slip; as an adjective it means nominal or merely symbolic.

clue.text: Whip accepting work with Young Conservatives is an imitator

indicators.note: the whip takes in, or accepts, the other pieces within it

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails, shortened to cat, is a whip
OP is short for opus, a work
YC abbreviates Young Conservatives, the youth wing of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A party whip who works with the youth wing is just copying someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests a parliamentary whip, but it is the lash called the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who slavishly copies another's behaviour or work.

clue.text: Worm found by queen once on hat

indicators.note: in a down clue the queen sits on top of the hat

parts.note: Anne was queen of Great Britain in the early 1700s
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A worm discovered sitting on a former queen's headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoological term: earthworms and leeches belong to this phylum of segmented worms.

clue.text: Source of Chardonnay — a very American drink

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Chardonnay grapes are the source of a drink from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Cava is Spanish sparkling wine, not American at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Spanish sparkling wine is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about love, duck?

indicators.note: the enthusiastic word goes around, or about, the love

parts.note: avid means keen or enthusiastic
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone keen on romance is a 'duck', a British term of endearment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' reads as a noun of affection, but it is the verb meaning dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to duck is to dodge or evade something.

clue.text: Taken out of the picture?

parts.note: literally, removed from a photograph by retouching with a fine spray of paint; normally the phrase means eliminated

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'taken out of the picture' means got rid of; here it is read literally of photo retouching.
explanation.definitionFit: Retouching a photo with a fine spray can erase a person or blemish from the image.

clue.text: Cooking in gas, try fish

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are mixed and prepared into something new

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: try cooking a fish on a gas hob.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flat cartilaginous sea creature with a venomous tail spine is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Picked up post and something for dinner

indicators.note: picked up as a signal or broadcast is heard, so the word sounds alike

parts.note: a stake is a post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: Collecting the mail and an item to eat for the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cut of beef is a typical main course at an evening meal.

clue.text: Cooked most of tripe and onion, getting wine

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: A dish of tripe and onion served with a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final E of tripe, giving TRIP; with ONION it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a red wine from a Burgundy grape variety is a kind of wine.

clue.text: Dry and press one, before short visit

indicators.note: the pressed pieces come before the visit

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to call is to pay a short visit

explanation.surface: Household chores: let something dry, press it, then pop out for a brief visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like laundry instruction but means wry, as in humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dry humour is wry and sardonic, saying the opposite of what is meant.

clue.text: Rejecting free article must be a low point

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to rid is to free
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Turning down a free newspaper piece marks a low ebb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the lowest point, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Letter supporting Germany is lacking consideration

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece lies underneath

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A letter backing Germany is said to show no regard for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being brusquely contemptuous shows no thought or regard for something.

clue.text: Be left in the air, struggling with no answer

indicators.note: struggling suggests things in disarray, so the letters are rearranged
with no signals that the answer's letter is excluded from the mix

explanation.surface: Being left up in the air and floundering without a solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' mixes the letters of IN THE AIR once A is set aside ('with no').
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic: to be left something in a will is to receive it as a legacy.

clue.text: Argued about when on weed regularly

parts.note: re means about or concerning
as can mean when

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone debated about when to put something on the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reasoned means argued logically, as a case presented with reasons.

clue.text: Travels after poor exam grades for mocks

indicators.note: the travels come after the grades

parts.note: D and E are low pass grades in British exams
rides means travels

explanation.surface: Bad marks in practice exams, which British students call mocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mocks' reads as practice exams, but it is the verb meaning ridicules.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mock is to ridicule or scorn someone.

clue.text: Cheating before spring, and making good progress

indicators.note: the cheating comes before the spring

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Someone cheats in spring and seems to be getting ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: thriving or prospering, advancing successfully.

clue.text: Note intended to keep detective

indicators.note: the intended word keeps, or holds, the detective inside

parts.note: meant means intended
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A message meant to retain an investigator.
explanation.definitionFit: Music theory: the third degree of a diatonic scale is a particular note.

clue.text: Short term career making patio

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to career is to race along

explanation.surface: A brief working career that results in a garden patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun for one's job, but it is the verb to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a paved outdoor area next to a house.

clue.text: Crazy way out covered by rent

indicators.note: the rent goes around, covering, the inner letters

parts.note: to hire is to rent

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An escape route funded by rental payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'way out', an exit, but it signals the letters of way being jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: gone wild or out of control, erratic.

clue.text: Sign off after concealed beatings

indicators.note: the rearranged sign comes after the concealed piece

parts.note: hid means concealed

indicators.note: off means the letters are spoiled, so reordered

explanation.surface: A sign-off after hidden thrashings.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thrashing or severe defeat, informal British usage.

clue.text: Small Oval ground producing such an outburst

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Oval, a London cricket ground, prompting a roar from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the cricket ground but rearranges OVAL into ALVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sudden burst of fire, applause or criticism.

clue.text: Time must be invested in genuine uprising in due course

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom upward
the time is put inside the genuine word

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: Political commentary: give a true revolt time and it will come eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts T in REAL, giving RETAL, and 'uprising' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: eventually, at some time afterwards.

clue.text: Hand in notice, besieging editor for new plan

indicators.note: the word surrounds, or besieges, the editor

parts.note: to resign is to hand in one's notice

explanation.surface: A journalist quits, crowding the editor, over a fresh plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a revised design or layout is a fresh plan.

clue.text: Pants regularly found in wrong material

indicators.note: the picked letters are found inside the wrong word

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Underwear made of an inappropriate fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a smooth glossy fabric is a kind of material.

clue.text: Energy drink gets youth initially nervous

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A young person gets jittery from an energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tense, irritable or on edge.

clue.text: By and large at sea?

definitions.meaning: literally, out on the ocean, the main being an old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic name for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning generally; literally, out on the open ocean.

clue.text: Daughter's after dainty fabric

indicators.note: the daughter's letter comes after the dainty word

parts.note: twee means excessively dainty or quaint
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A girl favours a delicate cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rough woollen cloth from Scotland is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Peer who's almost unprotected

indicators.note: unprotected means stripped of the outer letters that guard it

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A nobleman who is nearly defenceless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unprotected' looks like the definition, but it removes the outside letters of NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a British nobleman ranking above a viscount is a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Privately friendly, hugging Queen and heir

indicators.note: the friendly word hugs, or wraps around, the other pieces

parts.note: pally means friendly
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a son is an heir

explanation.surface: Being chummy in private with royalty and the next in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: done in one's own capacity rather than publicly or officially.
